intro: MQTT moves telemetry through a broker. A device publishes a message to a topic, a name like plant/inv1/telemetry. Every client that subscribed to a matching topic gets a copy. The sender and the readers never know each other.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: The gateway opens TCP to the broker on port 1883 and sends CONNECT. It leaves a will: a message the broker publishes for it if it vanishes.

online.title: Say online
online.text: The gateway publishes "online" to its status topic with the retain flag. The broker keeps the last retained message of every topic.

subscribe.title: Subscribe
subscribe.text: The dashboard, connected the same way, subscribes with a wildcard. The broker sends it the retained status at once.

publish.title: Publish
publish.text: The gateway publishes telemetry at QoS 1. Each hop has its own receipt: broker to gateway, then dashboard to broker. The gateway never learns who reads it.

keepalive.title: Keep alive
keepalive.text: Nothing to send for 60 s. The gateway sends PINGREQ, so the broker knows the connection is still alive.

lost.title: Gateway lost
lost.text: The gateway's link fails at 100 s, without a DISCONNECT. After 1.5 × the keep alive with nothing heard, the broker closes the connection and publishes the will.

frames.connect: I am plant-gw1. If I vanish, publish "offline" for me
frames.retained: The last status I kept: online

connect.name: CONNECT
connect.note: 0x10: packet type 1, CONNECT. The high 4 bits of the first byte are the type, the low 4 bits are flags.

rl-63.name: Remaining length
rl-63.note: 63 bytes follow. A length below 128 fits in one byte.

protocol.name: Protocol name
protocol.note: "MQTT", after its length 0x0004. Every text in MQTT starts with a 2-byte length.

flags.name: Connect flags
flags.note: 0xEE: a user name and a password follow, the will is retained (bit 5) and sent at QoS 1 (bits 4-3), there is a will (bit 2), and clean session (bit 1): start without old subscriptions.

keepalive.name: Keep alive
keepalive.note: 60 s. The gateway promises to send something at least once a minute.

client-id.name: Client ID
client-id.note: "plant-gw1". The broker knows each client by this ID, so it must be unique.

will-topic.name: Will topic
will-topic.note: plant/gw1/status: where the broker publishes the will if the gateway vanishes.

password.name: Password
password.note: "Gw1-p4ss", readable by anyone on the path: on port 1883 nothing is encrypted.

session-present.name: Session present
session-present.note: 0: the broker holds no old session for this client.

return-code.name: Return code
return-code.note: 0: connection accepted. 4 would mean a wrong user name or password, 5 not authorized.

publish-q1-retain.name: PUBLISH
publish-q1-retain.note: 0x33: PUBLISH (type 3), QoS 1 (bits 2-1) and retain (bit 0): the broker keeps this message for clients that subscribe later.

id-1-gateway.name: Packet id 1
id-1-gateway.note: A QoS 1 message carries a number, so that its receipt can name it.

online.name: Payload
online.note: "online". MQTT does not care what the payload means: the clients agree on that.

puback.name: PUBACK
puback.note: 0x40: the receipt for a QoS 1 PUBLISH.

id-1-ack.name: Packet id 1
id-1-ack.note: Message 1 has arrived: the gateway can forget it.

subscribe.name: SUBSCRIBE
subscribe.note: 0x82: SUBSCRIBE (type 8). Its low 4 bits must be 0010.

id-1-subscribe.name: Packet id 1
id-1-subscribe.note: Picked by the dashboard. Each client numbers its own packets.

filter-telemetry.name: Topic filter
filter-telemetry.note: plant/+/telemetry: the telemetry of every device in the plant.

want-qos-1.name: QoS 1
want-qos-1.note: The highest QoS the dashboard wants for this filter.

filter-status.name: Topic filter
filter-status.note: plant/+/status: the status of every gateway.

want-qos-0.name: QoS 0
want-qos-0.note: At most once, without a receipt: enough for a status.

granted.name: Return codes
granted.note: One per filter, in order: QoS 1 granted, QoS 0 granted. 0x80 would mean refused.

publish-q0-retain.name: PUBLISH
publish-q0-retain.note: 0x31: PUBLISH at QoS 0 with the retain flag set: a stored message, not a new one.

rl-24.name: Remaining length
rl-24.note: 24 bytes follow. A QoS 0 message has no packet id.

online-kept.name: Payload
online-kept.note: "online", sent by the gateway 8 s earlier. The dashboard gets the status now instead of at the next change. It comes at QoS 0, the lower of the two QoS levels.

rl-129.name: Remaining length
rl-129.note: 129 bytes follow. Each length byte holds 7 bits, lowest part first; a top bit of 1 means another byte follows. 0x81 0x01 = 1 + 1 × 128.

json-ts.name: Payload · time
json-ts.note: {"ts":"2026-11-12T10:41:07.280Z", when the gateway read the values. The JSON format is the gateway's choice: MQTT carries any bytes.

json-values.name: Payload · values
json-values.note: Active power 4820.5 kW, reactive power 610.2 kvar, voltage 20150 V, frequency 50.01 Hz.

id-2-ack.name: Packet id 2
id-2-ack.note: Received: the broker is now responsible for the message.

id-1-broker.name: Packet id 1
id-1-broker.note: The broker numbers what it sends to each client itself. The gateway's 2 belongs to the gateway's link only.

publish-q0.name: PUBLISH
publish-q0.note: 0x30: QoS 0 and no retain flag. The will was set with QoS 1 and retain, but the dashboard asked for QoS 0 on this filter, and a message for an existing subscription never has the retain flag set.

offline.name: Payload
offline.note: "offline", the will from the CONNECT. The broker also keeps it as the topic's new retained message.

a-site.name: Site
a-site.note: Levels go from wide to narrow, separated by /.

a-device.name: Device
a-device.note: The device the data is about.

a-data.name: Data
a-data.note: What kind of data it is.

a-plus.name: Wildcard
a-plus.note: + matches exactly one level: inv1, inv2, gw1 … # matches all levels below and must come last: plant/#.

facts.standard: MQTT 3.1.1 (OASIS 2014, also ISO/IEC 20922). MQTT 5.0 adds reason codes and properties.
facts.between: Clients (gateways, dashboards, apps) and a broker. Clients never talk to each other directly.
facts.security: TLS on TCP 8883, with a password or a client certificate
facts.frames: CONNECT, PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE and their receipts; PINGREQ to keep alive

tips: Port 1883 sends everything in clear text, the password too: look at the CONNECT bytes. Outside a closed network, use TLS on port 8883.
Two clients with the same client ID push each other off: the broker drops the older connection. Two gateways cloned from one image then kick each other out all day.
QoS 1 means at least once. After a reconnect the same message can arrive twice, so a subscriber must cope with duplicates.
A retained message stays until it is replaced. To delete it, publish an empty retained message to the same topic.

anatomy.topic: A topic: levels from wide to narrow
anatomy.filter: A filter with a wildcard, and the topics it matches

timing.title: When the broker gives up on a client
timing.note: The broker restarts a timer with every packet from the gateway. When 1.5 × the keep alive (90 s) pass in silence, it publishes the will: here 65 s after the link failed. A shorter keep alive finds a dead client sooner, but costs more traffic.

playground.file: The broker's configuration (Mosquitto 2). Pick a marked line to see what it does.
playground.anonymous: Clients without a user name are refused.
playground.passwords: The user names and their hashed passwords, made with mosquitto_passwd.
playground.acl: Which topics each user may publish to or subscribe to. Give the gateway only its own topics, and the dashboard read access only.
playground.plain: Plain MQTT on port 1883, listening only on the broker's address in the plant network.
playground.tls: MQTT over TLS on port 8883. The broker proves who it is with its certificate; clients check it against the CA.
playground.persistence: Writes retained messages and sessions to disk. Without it, a restart forgets every retained status.
